executiveSummary: GM1659's identity, Brabant-Zuidoost safety-region assignment, full 2025 boundary and CBS resident control are coherent. Fresh context reports 23,324 residents; fifteen published neighbourhood rows sum to 23,335 (+11, +0.047%), a negligible difference that preserves CBS rounding and suppression semantics. The bundle contains four districts, fifteen neighbourhoods, four BAG places, 23 BRT settlement labels, four logical N-road records, no ProRail station and 49 scheduled-transit stop areas. All ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services and pass structural/numerical contracts. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Zuidoost places the region outside direct Rhine/Meuse/sea flooding and identifies the Aa and smaller streams as the relevant high-water pathways, while the generic major-river preset applies 0.750748 normalized inundation stress at T+24 and T+72, growing affected residents from 4,641 to 5,210 without a selected Aa/Goorloop/Snelleloop/Boerdonkse Aa event, footprint, controls, arrival or recession. The value is normalized stress, never 0.75 physical metres. Nine unrelated presets reuse exactly the same complete neighbourhood order. Public Waterinfo points at Aarle-Rixtel and Sluis 6 are timestamped observations, not a flood surface or T+72 forecast; 105 registered water objects do not supply topology or live state. A published Aa en Maas control-system replacement demonstrates that cyber–water-control dependencies are real but does not identify current compromise or validate exact Drainage loss. The N279/N272/N615 skeleton omits the Beekse Brug and local canal crossings, rural approaches, bus operation and the cross-boundary route to Elkerliek Helmond. Exact utility, care, supply and recovery trajectories lack verified topology, capacity, backup, resources and actions. Empty local warning, road, care, air, seismic and government screens are Unknown/NoData, never zero or safe.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The official municipality row identifies GM1659 Laarbeek and reports 23,324 residents, density 421 per square kilometre, 24.6% age 65 or older and 2,928 one-person households.

The fifteen published neighbourhood rows sum to 23,335 residents (+11, +0.047%), 9,915 households and 5,750 residents aged 65 or older; the negligible difference retains annual rounding and suppression semantics.

Most statistics cover all fifteen neighbourhoods; home-value and housing-tenure fields cover 13/15, cars per household and benefit/pension fields 12/15, while district-heating share and public-charging counts cover zero rows and must not become zero.

CBS OData is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0, with quarterly additions described for this annual table. It controls resident allocation, not incident-time presence, self-reliance, pupils, patients, workforce, visitors, agricultural activity, livestock or deprivation.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Full municipal geometry, settlements and road, rail and scheduled-transit reference inputs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary/statistics and current generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS reference snapshots
supports: The generated centre [5.609568713809628, 51.53364302949722] lies inside the fresh 2025 municipal boundary.

The bundle retains four districts, fifteen neighbourhoods, four BAG places—Aarle-Rixtel, Beek en Donk, Lieshout and Mariahout—and 23 BRT labels: four woonkernen, two deelkernen, six gehuchten and eleven buurtschappen.

Four logical road records identify N279 north/south plus N272 and N615 links to four neighbouring municipalities. The two N279 records share physical corridor NWB-road-279 and are series sections, not independent additive capacity.

No ProRail station lies inside GM1659 and 49 GTFS stop areas are assigned. Static geometry/timetables do not prove incident-time road/bus operation, canal-crossing state, rural access, emergency priority, destination or throughput.

CBS boundary OGC is half-yearly/CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark 1.0; BRT is CC BY 4.0; NWB is monthly/CC0 1.0; ProRail is manually refreshed/CC0 1.0. OVapi GTFS is free-use best-effort context without an operational SLA.
Nominal values of 150 are generalized scenario units and N279 series links must never be summed as parallel capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Laarbeek climate stress test, adaptation agenda and current municipal climate context
evidenceSources.edition: 2019 DPRA stress test and current implementation/adaptation pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Laarbeek, five other Peel municipalities, Aa en Maas and Brabant Water use regional stress testing and risk dialogues for heat, drought and water-overlast adaptation; the programme identifies more than one hundred projects and highlights 21 for follow-up.

The municipality provides a report and map for the climate stress test and says climate risks affect health, nature, economy and liveability. These are official scenarios/planning layers, not incident observations, probability estimates or arbitrary T+72 forcing.

Projects carry owner, location and programme timing, but completion and current performance can differ by edition. A programme item cannot silently become a completed protection or operational action.

The public pages/PDF route does not state a standard reusable machine-data licence, guaranteed refresh cadence, native raster CRS/units or NoData contract; these must be resolved before simulation use.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Aa en Maas / Het Waterschapshuis / Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Aa, Goorloop, Snelleloop and Boerdonkse Aa system, control projects and public water observations/assets
evidenceSources.edition: Current water-board project pages; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026; Waterinfo observations retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Aa en Maas identifies the Aa, Snelleloop and Boerdonkse Aa around Beek en Donk as a linked beekdal and completed about six kilometres of 2025–2026 reconfiguration for better handling of dry and wet periods. The work's lifecycle and geometry must be versioned rather than assumed from an old baseline.

Official system analysis says the Boerdonkse Aa, Goorloop and Donkersvoortse Loop converge into the Aa across a broad, historically inundated valley with small gradient and regulated flow through culverts and siphons. This is the relevant local mechanism, not direct Rhine/Meuse depth.

The water board reported in June 2026 that its remote TMX system operates weirs, pumps, fish passes, gates, measurement points and rack cleaners and that the head-end needs replacement after supplier failure. This proves a managed/control dependency and continuity project, not current cyber compromise, command state or failure.

Seven fresh Waterinfo observations at 2 September 2026 17:20–17:30 UTC cover discharge at Schabbert outlet and Sluis 6 inlet/outlet plus water levels above/below those locations. They are point observations under CC0, not a flood surface, threshold judgement, forecast or T+72 state.

The deployment HWH/PDOK screen returns 105 points: five sewer pumps, eleven surface-water pumps, one wastewater-treatment point and 88 weirs. The aggregation is partial/contributor-dependent under CC BY-SA 4.0 and does not establish catchments, connectivity, comparable capacity, settings, power/backup, control or live operation.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, crisis organisation and first-72-hour preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk profile 2025–2028; current crisis-plan and national preparedness pages
supports: VRBZO states that Zuidoost-Brabant's higher topographic position places it outside direct sea and major-river flooding; regional high-water problems concern the Aa and smaller streams and possible drainage blockage when northern Brabant floods.

The risk profile distinguishes extreme precipitation, smaller-water high levels, regional-defence failure, nature fire, storm, heat, winter weather, utility/cyber disruption and hazardous-material events. It treats nature-fire spread as dependent on vegetation, weather, access, water and use; a regional risk is not a current local ignition.
The regional crisis plan describes organisation, responsibilities and authorities for crisis management. It is planning/governance evidence, not a live staffing, resource, action or incident feed.

Current national guidance advises a 72-hour emergency kit including three litres of water per person per day, food, medicine, radio/power and a personal plan because power, water and internet may fail. Guidance does not prove household preparation or supply availability.
The regional PDF/pages and Rijksoverheid guidance do not expose a stable machine-readable local resource/action API or blanket machine reuse contract in the inspected responses.

evidenceSources.edition: LIWO release 2025.1.6; deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: LIWO 2025.1.6 provides downloadable professional flood layers requiring specialist water-manager interpretation. A selected case must retain source, boundary/defence/control state, footprint, native units/resolution, arrival/persistence/recession, probability, CRS, licence and NoData.

No KNMI weather station is assigned inside GM1659 and the 48-hour warning retrieval has no warning records. No-warning is issue-time provincial context, not gridded local forcing or an all-clear for arbitrary exercises.

No Waterinfo forecast point is assigned despite seven current observations. Missing forecast locations/horizons remain NoData; observations cannot be extrapolated through T+72 without a hydraulic model.

The NDW snapshot published 2 September 2026 15:25 UTC assigns no situation inside GM1659. Its CC0, 72-hour current-situation screen is not exhaustive proof that routes or bridges are open and must apply only to an overlapping exercise clock.
KNMI sources are CC BY 4.0, Waterinfo and NDW CC0 unless stated. Every record needs issue/observation/valid/retrieval time, coverage, revision/fault state and affectsSimulation.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — N279/N615 and Beekse Brug constraints with cross-boundary acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Province notice 15 January 2026; current provider pages; RIVM questionnaire 2026 v1.1

The generated graph represents N279/N272/N615 boundary links but not Beekse Brug, Donkse Brug and other Zuid-Willemsvaart crossings as typed internal structures with opening, mode, direction, queues, restriction or failure state.

RIVM's 2026 v1.1 national screen assigns no emergency department inside GM1659. Elkerliek Helmond is about 6.15 kilometres straight-line from the representative centre and reports a 24/7 emergency department, acute obstetrics, twelve treatment rooms and 14,251 visits in 2025.

A straight-line distance and annual provider/questionnaire statements do not prove route time, ambulance availability, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, generator endurance or incident capacity. RIVM data are CC0 1.0; provider/project pages state no machine reuse licence.

No selected Aa en Maas/WMCN/LIWO case establishes a GM1659 Aa/Goorloop/Snelleloop/Boerdonkse Aa boundary, defence/control state, footprint, depth/velocity, arrival or recession. A generic value is not evidence and no selected case is not safe.

Municipal stress-test products are valuable official scenario/planning evidence but need native machine files, edition, CRS, event/antecedent conditions, units, licence and explicit NoData before analytical use.

Aa en Maas's TMX replacement describes a real control dependency and project, not current compromise, asset failure, control command, manual fallback or operator restoration commitment. Sensitive topology must not be reconstructed publicly.

Seven Waterinfo points are observations valid only at their locations/timestamps and no local forecast is assigned. They cannot be spatialized or extrapolated to T+72 without an authority model; absent horizons remain NoData.
The Beekse Brug plan and observed queue mechanism do not establish current closure, capacity or completed improvement. Exercise use requires confirmed state and valid-time overlap.

CBS residents omit pupils, patients, care residents, workers, visitors, road/canal users, agricultural activity/livestock, volunteers and responders. Rounded/suppressed aggregates cannot identify individual needs or event presence.

RIVM/Elkerliek pages do not expose incident-time ambulance availability, staffing, dispatch, hospital acceptance, occupancy, backup or restoration; protected operational information must not be inferred.
NWB and GTFS do not prove scenario-time road, bridge or bus operation, emergency priority, accessibility, detours, destination or throughput. N279 series links are not independent redundancy.

No explicit current ignition, perimeter or remote plume supports the wildfire output. Regional nature risk and municipal forests cannot become a local smoke forecast without source/time/wind geometry.
One Enexis planning sample, water objects, antennas and schools have different support, cadence and licences and remain affectsSimulation=false without reviewed causal bindings.

No-warning and no locally assigned NDW, care, PM2.5, weather-station, seismic, government or forecast point are coverage/time facts, not zero hazard, disruption, pollution, need or service continuity.

Exact hazard, affected-population, service, recovery and person-hour outputs remain synthetic exercises, not observations, forecasts, operator commitments or decision-grade advice until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the case.
This audit covers only the first 72 hours. Flooding, drought, agricultural/livestock effects, care interruption, contamination and infrastructure recovery can persist much longer.
